media.title: Polydor 10237-B — “Song Is Ended,” Hermann Bick and Dr. Kaper
media.description: Reduced-resolution documentary image of the label of a Japanese Polydor pressing of “Song Is Ended.” The label credits Hermann Bick and Dr. Kaper as a two-piano jazz duo and gives catalogue number 10237-B and matrix 1774 BK. The image supports the documented history of Kaper’s late-1920s jazz-piano partnership; it is not an audio asset.
media.altText: Black-and-gold Polydor record label for “Song Is Ended,” crediting Hermann Bick and Dr. Kaper on two pianos; catalogue 10237-B.
media.rightsNote: The YouTube page supplies no licence or photographer credit for the record-label image. Photographer and image rights holder are unknown. timelineEvents.title: Jazz Piano Partnership
timelineEvents.label: 1928 · Jazz piano partnership
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Kaper records jazz-influenced piano duo arrangements with Hermann Bick for Polydor.
timelineEvents.longDescription: Along with Hermann Bick (Bieck), he records piano duo arrangements for Deutsche Grammophon/Polydor. These sessions showcase contemporary American jazz standards including "Miss Annabelle Lee," "The Varsity Drag," and "The Song Is Ended." The collaboration blends classical virtuosity with jazz spontaneity, creating sophisticated interpretations that avoid the trivial "novelty piano" style of the era.
